name: singapore
title: Singapore
note: About 2,300 mm of rain a year in short, intense convective bursts. The interesting case for this product: Singapore has one of the best drainage networks in the world, and we have no drainage data for it at all. Our screening should therefore overstate pooling here more than anywhere else — which is exactly the limit we disclose on every run, now visible rather than theoretical.

terrain.source: DeltaDTM v1.1 (Pronk et al. 2024), via Earth Engine community catalog
terrain.note: Raw band. Non-finite is sea or outside coverage; the value 30 is the model's cap.

population.note: Total population spread across near-complete OSM footprints. The staged box includes a thin strip of Johor across the strait, which slightly dilutes the ratio - a conservative bias. An order of magnitude for who is exposed, by area.

news_query: Singapore (flood OR flooding OR "flash flood" OR "heavy rain" OR ponding OR waterlogging)

surface_heat.source: Landsat 8 and 9 Collection 2 Level 2 surface temperature (USGS), via Earth Engine
surface_heat.licence: USGS Landsat data are public domain
surface_heat.season: all months of the year, as Singapore has no dry season
surface_heat.composite: median of every clear view; cloud, cirrus, shadow and water masked
surface_heat.resolution: the thermal sensor resolves patches about 100 m across; USGS delivers it resampled to a 30 m grid, and this is on the terrain's 1 arcsec grid
surface_heat.grid: the staged terrain's own 1 arcsec grid, nearest neighbour from Landsat's 30 m
surface_heat.unit: degrees C of the SURFACE, not the air
caveats: A typical-season picture, not a forecast and not today.
Surface temperature, the skin of roofs, roads and leaves. In sun it runs well above air temperature and is not comparable with a forecast figure.
Landsat passes at mid-morning. Afternoon surfaces run hotter and spread further apart.
The thermal sensor sees patches about 100 m across, so this shows a few blocks at best and never a single building or roof.
Water is masked: this is a picture of land.
